name: reply-tierlist-getting-started
description: >-
  First-run onboarding for the X Reply Tierlist bot. Use on the user's first

---
# Getting started

Always reply in the user's language. Keep it short. This bot is free: it only reads public X data through the built-in X access, so the user never connects an X account or spends credits.

1. **Say what the bot does (one line):** "I turn your X replies into a tierlist – the accounts you reply to most, ranked S to F in one clean image. Free, no X login needed."
2. **Ask for their X handle** (one short line, plain text) unless they already gave it in this chat. Don't assume it from context without their confirmation. Check it with the built-in `x.get_users_by_username`.
   - Found and public: continue.
   - Not found: ask them to double-check the spelling.
   - Protected/private or public reads unavailable: offer the fallback – upload their X Analytics content export (CSV, from x.com → Analytics → Content → Export) and continue with step 3b of the `reply-tierlist` skill.
3. **Ask the quick questions, one widget at a time:** Zeitraum (7 / **30** / 90 Tage / 1 Jahr), Größe (48 / **60** Accounts, square image), Look (**Dark** / Light). Never add other questions (e.g. which replies to analyse) – it always ranks the user's own replies to others. No exclude question – spam/adult accounts are filtered automatically, and the user can name exclusions in chat.
4. **Run the first tierlist** with the `reply-tierlist` skill (progress line → fetch → PNG → share/GIF widget).

Free: uses only the built-in public X reads. Use when the user asks for a reply tierlist or "who do I reply to most".

---
name: reply-tierlist
description: >-
  Build an "X Reply Tierlist" for any public X account - ranks the 48 or 60
  accounts it replied to most (default last 30 days) into full S-F rows in a
  dark or light look, sends a downloadable square PNG, optionally a reveal GIF,
  and share links. Free: uses only the built-in public X reads. Use when the
  user asks for a reply tierlist or "who do I reply to most".
---
# Reply Tierlist

Always answer in the user's language. Keep messages short. Never post to X; the user shares the image themselves.
Cost to the user: **nothing**. Use only the built-in public X namespace `x` (no user connection, no credits). Never call the user's own X connector (`user-X`) for this skill and never ask the user to connect X.

## 1. Questions before generating
- **Handle:** if you don't know the user's X handle, ask for it in one short line (plain text). Never assume it from context (profile, earlier chats) without the user confirming it.
Then ask exactly three quick choice widgets, **one at a time** (labels in the user's language). Skip any that the user already answered:
1. **Zeitraum / Range:** `7 Tage`, `30 Tage` (default, preselect), `90 Tage`, `1 Jahr`.
2. **Größe / Size:** `48 Accounts` (6 rows × 8, bigger avatars) or `60 Accounts` (6 × 10). Default 60. Both give a 1:1 square image (PNG and GIF).
3. **Look:** `Dark` (black, X blue, white) or `Light` (white, X blue, black text). Default Dark.
Ask nothing else: always analyse the user's own replies to other accounts. Never invent extra questions (e.g. which replies to analyse or a specific post). No exclude question. Automatically drop obvious spam/adult accounts you notice in the results (e.g. porn-site handles) and mention it in one line; if the user names accounts to exclude in chat, add them too. Both go into `exclude`.

## 2. Progress line
Send one short line, e.g. "Reading your replies from the last 30 days and building the tierlist… (~4–5 min)". Nothing else until the result.

## 3. Fetch data (free namespace `x`)
Free-path limits: **25 results per call, 30 calls/minute, 1,000 calls/day** (shared across this user's requests). Every result shows "X reads left".
Use **date-windowed search** – it can jump straight to any point in the range (works back 2+ years). `get_users_posts` is not suitable: it only reaches the latest ~3,200 posts.

1. `x.get_users_by_username` with `username` = handle → `ID`. Not found or protected: say so and stop (or offer the CSV fallback, 3b).
2. Split `[now − range, now]` into equal windows, one call each (cap ≈ 130 calls per run):

   | Range | Window width | Calls | Runtime (≈30/min) | Label |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | 30 days (default) | 6 h | 120 | ~4–5 min | Last 30 days |
   | 7 days | 6 h | 28 | < 1 min | Last 7 days |
   | 90 days | 18 h | 120 | ~4–5 min | Last 90 days |
   | 1 year | 3 days | 122 | ~4–5 min | Last 1 year |

3. For each window call `x.search_posts_all` with `write_to_file: true`:
   - `query`: `from:HANDLE is:reply`
   - `start_time` / `end_time`: the window (ISO `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`; clamp the last window to now), `max_results`: 25
   - `post.fields`: `in_reply_to_user_id,created_at`, `expansions`: `in_reply_to_user_id`, `user.fields`: `username`
   Save each file to `/workspace/reply-tierlist/pages/`. Issue up to ~28 calls in parallel per batch, then wait until the minute resets (time is in the result / error) before the next batch – never retry in a loop.
   - A window that returns a `next_token` had more than 25 replies; **don't page it** (keeps the call count fixed). The run is then a time-even **sample**, which ranks frequent repliers well.
   - If remaining daily reads are fewer than the planned calls, use wider windows so the whole range is still covered, and say so in one line.
4. Aggregate (RANGE_START / RANGE_END = first window's start / last window's end, LABEL from the table):

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, glob, collections
ME="ID"; HANDLE="HANDLE"; N=80; LABEL="Last 30 days"   # keep extra rows so exclusions still fill all rows
RANGE_START="YYYY-MM-DD"; RANGE_END="YYYY-MM-DD"
c=collections.Counter(); users={}; seen=set(); sat=0; win=0
for p in glob.glob('/workspace/reply-tierlist/pages/*'):
    s=open(p).read()
    if '{"' not in s: continue
    d=json.loads(s[s.index('{"'):s.rindex('}')+1]); win+=1
    if d.get('meta',{}).get('next_token'): sat+=1
    for u in d.get('includes',{}).get('users',[]): users[u['id']]=u['username']
    for t in d.get('data',[]):
        if t['id'] in seen: continue
        seen.add(t['id'])
        k=t.get('in_reply_to_user_id')
        if k and k!=ME: c[k]+=1
ranked=[[users[k],v] for k,v in c.most_common() if k in users][:N]
json.dump({"handle":HANDLE,"since":RANGE_START,"until":RANGE_END,"range_label":LABEL,
           "replies":len(seen),"sampled":sat>0,"ranked":ranked,
           "size":SIZE, "theme":"THEME", "exclude":EXCLUDE},   # e.g. 60, "dark", ["spamhandle"]
          open('/workspace/reply-tierlist/input.json','w'))
print(win,"windows,",sat,"sampled,",len(seen),"replies,",len(ranked),"ranked")
PY
```
The header reads e.g. `Last 30 days · 15 Sep 2026 – 15 Oct 2026 · sampled · 1,459 replies` ("sampled" only when at least one window was capped). If the run stopped before covering the whole range, set RANGE_START to the earliest window actually fetched and add one honest line in chat ("covered X of Y days"). Self-replies are excluded. Before ranking, drop obvious spam, bot or adult accounts (e.g. handles or names clearly referencing porn/XXX/NSFW, or known spam) and any accounts the user asked to exclude; fill the slots with the next accounts. With fewer accounts than the chosen size, the renderer spreads them evenly over the six rows; if that happens, mention it in one line or suggest a smaller size.

## 3b. Fallback: X Analytics CSV
If the free reads fail (account protected, limits exhausted) or the user prefers it, ask them to upload their X Analytics content export (x.com → Analytics → Content → Export, CSV). Then build `input.json` from it:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import csv, re, collections, json, sys
P="/path/to/upload.csv"; HANDLE="HANDLE"; N=80
rows=list(csv.DictReader(open(P, encoding="utf-8-sig")))
tcol=next(k for k in rows[0] if re.search(r"(post|tweet).*text|^text$", k, re.I))
dcol=next((k for k in rows[0] if re.search(r"date|time", k, re.I)), None)
c=collections.Counter(); dates=[]
for r in rows:
    m=re.match(r"^((?:@\w+\s+)+)", r[tcol] or "")
    if not m: continue
    h=re.findall(r"@(\w+)", m.group(1))[0]
    if h.lower()==HANDLE.lower(): continue
    c[h]+=1
    if dcol and r[dcol]: dates.append(r[dcol][:10])
json.dump({"handle":HANDLE,"since":min(dates) if dates else "","until":max(dates) if dates else "",
           "range_label":"X Analytics export","replies":sum(c.values()),"ranked":[[h,v] for h,v in c.most_common(N)]}, open('/workspace/reply-tierlist/input.json','w'))
print(sum(c.values()),"replies from",len(rows),"rows")
PY
```
The leading @handle of a reply is counted as the replied-to account (best effort; column names vary by export, adjust if needed).

## 4. Render
On first run write the renderer (below) to `/workspace/reply-tierlist/render.py` if missing, then:
```bash
cd /workspace/reply-tierlist && python3 render.py input.json tierlist --size 60 --theme dark
```
`--size 48|60` (6 full rows of 8 / 10, always a 1:1 square), `--theme dark|light`, `--no-gif` to skip the GIF. Writes `tierlist.png` (1080×1080) and `tierlist.gif` (~5 s drop-in reveal) in the chosen look. Avatars come from unavatar.io (3 tries) with an initials-tile fallback. Needs Pillow + requests (auto-installed). Look at the PNG once before sending.

## 5. Send the PNG
Send `tierlist.png` as a file attachment (the main download), with one short line naming the S tier's top 3.

## 6. Share + extras (one widget)
Right after the PNG, offer a choice widget (labels in the user's language):
- **Nur Post teilen** (share post only) → send `https://x.com/intent/post?text=<url-encoded text>` with a short text, e.g. "My X reply tierlist for the last 30 days 👀"
- **Mit Top-Handles taggen** (tag top handles) → same link, text plus the top 3–5 S-tier handles, e.g. "My X reply tierlist 👀 S tier: @a @b @c"
- **Reveal-GIF** → send `tierlist.gif` as a file attachment.
With each share link add: the image isn't attached automatically – download the PNG and attach it to the post yourself. Don't send the GIF unless asked.

## Renderer (write to /workspace/reply-tierlist/render.py)
```bash
mkdir -p /workspace/reply-tierlist/pages
cat > /workspace/reply-tierlist/render.py <<'RENDER_PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""X Reply Tierlist renderer. Pillow + requests only.
Usage: python3 render.py input.json [out_basename] [--size 48|60] [--theme dark|light] [--no-gif]
input.json: {"handle":"name","since":"YYYY-MM-DD","until":"YYYY-MM-DD",
             "ranked":[["handle",count],...], "range_label": "Last 30 days", "replies": 1459, "sampled": true}  (optional, shown in header),
             "size": 60, "theme": "dark", "exclude": ["handle", ...]}   (optional; CLI flags win)
ranked = most replies first. Output is always a 1:1 square; rows are always full: 48 = 6x8, 60 = 6x10.
Writes <out>.png and <out>.gif (default: tierlist)."""
import sys, json, io, os, math, hashlib, datetime as dt
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
try:
    import requests
except ImportError:
    os.system(f"{sys.executable} -m pip install -q requests"); import requests
try:
    from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
except ImportError:
    os.system(f"{sys.executable} -m pip install -q Pillow"); from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

BLUE = (29, 155, 240)
THEMES = {
    "dark":  dict(bg=(0, 0, 0), fg=(255, 255, 255), dim=(113, 118, 123), line=(32, 35, 39), tile=(22, 24, 28)),
    "light": dict(bg=(255, 255, 255), fg=(15, 20, 25), dim=(83, 100, 113), line=(230, 233, 236), tile=(239, 243, 244)),
}
BLACK, WHITE, DIM, LINE, TILE_BG = [THEMES["dark"][k] for k in ("bg", "fg", "dim", "line", "tile")]
SIZES = {48: 8, 60: 10}                 # people -> avatars per row (6 full rows, square image)

def set_theme(name):
    global BLACK, WHITE, DIM, LINE, TILE_BG
    BLACK, WHITE, DIM, LINE, TILE_BG = [THEMES[name][k] for k in ("bg", "fg", "dim", "line", "tile")]
TIERS = ["S", "A", "B", "C", "D", "F"]
PER_ROW, MAX_PEOPLE = 10, 60          # set from size in render()
CACHE = "/tmp/reply-tierlist-avatars"

FONT_PATHS = ["/usr/share/fonts/truetype/sand-box/google/Inter/Inter-VariableFont_opsz,wght.ttf",
              "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/inter/Inter-Bold.ttf",
              "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf",
              "/Library/Fonts/Arial Bold.ttf", "C:/Windows/Fonts/arialbd.ttf"]

def font(size, weight="Bold"):
    for p in FONT_PATHS:
        if os.path.exists(p):
            f = ImageFont.truetype(p, size)
            try: f.set_variation_by_name(weight)
            except Exception: pass
            return f
    return ImageFont.load_default(size)

def split(n):
    """Fill tiers top-down evenly: 60 -> 10 per tier; fewer -> as even as possible."""
    n = min(n, MAX_PEOPLE)
    return [n // 6 + (1 if i < n % 6 else 0) for i in range(6)]

def initials_tile(h, sz):
    im = Image.new("RGB", (sz, sz), TILE_BG); d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    d.text((sz / 2, sz / 2), h[:2].upper(), font=font(int(sz * .38)), fill=BLUE, anchor="mm")
    return im

def avatar(h, sz):
    os.makedirs(CACHE, exist_ok=True)
    p = os.path.join(CACHE, hashlib.md5(h.lower().encode()).hexdigest() + ".png")
    try:
        if not os.path.exists(p):
            for attempt in range(3):  # unavatar sometimes fails transiently
                r = requests.get(f"https://unavatar.io/x/{h}?fallback=false", timeout=20,
                                 headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"})
                if r.ok: break
            r.raise_for_status()
            Image.open(io.BytesIO(r.content)).convert("RGB").save(p)
        im = Image.open(p).convert("RGB")
        w, hh = im.size; m = min(w, hh)
        im = im.crop(((w - m) // 2, (hh - m) // 2, (w + m) // 2, (hh + m) // 2))
        return im.resize((sz, sz), Image.LANCZOS), True
    except Exception:
        return initials_tile(h, sz), False

def round_mask(sz, r, ss=4):
    m = Image.new("L", (sz * ss, sz * ss), 0)
    ImageDraw.Draw(m).rounded_rectangle((0, 0, sz * ss - 1, sz * ss - 1), r * ss, fill=255)
    return m.resize((sz, sz), Image.LANCZOS)

def fmt_date(s):
    try: return dt.date.fromisoformat(s[:10]).strftime("%d %b %Y").lstrip("0")
    except Exception: return s

def layout(data, S=1.0):
    """Square canvas (W = H). Six tier rows, each exactly one full row of PER_ROW avatars."""
    W = H = int(1080 * S); pad = int(40 * S); lab = int(72 * S)
    head = int(196 * S); foot = int(78 * S); min_gap = int(10 * S)
    per = PER_ROW
    avail_w = W - 2 * pad - lab
    row_h = (H - head - foot) // 6
    tile_w = (avail_w - min_gap * per) // per
    tile_h = int((row_h - 2 * int(12 * S)) / 1.22)          # tile + caption (~22%) + padding
    tile = min(tile_w, tile_h)
    cap = max(int(22 * S), int(tile * .22))
    gap = (avail_w - per * tile) / per                       # justify across the full width
    ranked = data["ranked"][:MAX_PEOPLE]; sizes = split(len(ranked))
    tiers, i = [], 0
    for n in sizes: tiers.append(ranked[i:i + n]); i += n
    y = head; rows = []; slots = []
    for t, people in zip(TIERS, tiers):
        rows.append((t, y, row_h))
        top = y + (row_h - tile - cap) // 2
        for j, (hd, c) in enumerate(people[:per]):
            x = int(pad + lab + gap / 2 + j * (tile + gap))
            slots.append((t, hd, c, x, top))
        y += row_h
    return dict(W=W, H=H, pad=pad, lab=lab, tile=tile, gap=gap, rows=rows, slots=slots, S=S, head=head)

def spaced(d, xy, text, f, fill, track):
    """Draw letter-spaced text starting at xy (left, middle)."""
    x, y = xy
    for ch in text:
        d.text((x, y), ch, font=f, fill=fill, anchor="lm")
        x += d.textlength(ch, font=f) + track
    return x

def pill(d, x, cy, text, f, S, fill=None, outline=None, color=None):
    """Rounded pill left-aligned at x, vertically centred on cy. Returns right edge."""
    w = d.textlength(text, font=f) + int(28 * S); h = int(34 * S)
    d.rounded_rectangle((x, cy - h // 2, x + w, cy + h // 2), h // 2, fill=fill,
                        outline=outline, width=max(1, int(1.5 * S)))
    d.text((x + w / 2, cy), text, font=f, fill=color, anchor="mm")
    return x + w

def base(data, L):
    S, W, H, pad = L["S"], L["W"], L["H"], L["pad"]
    img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BLACK); d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    # header: eyebrow, handle, chips (range label, dates, sample size)
    spaced(d, (pad, int(46 * S)), "REPLY TIERLIST", font(int(15 * S), "Bold"), BLUE, int(2.4 * S))
    d.text((pad - int(2 * S), int(94 * S)), "@" + data["handle"].lstrip("@"), font=font(int(54 * S), "Bold"),
           fill=WHITE, anchor="lm")
    cy = int(152 * S); fchip = font(int(16 * S), "SemiBold")
    x = pill(d, pad, cy, data.get("range_label") or "Reply Tierlist", fchip, S, fill=BLUE, color=(255, 255, 255))
    dates = f"{fmt_date(data.get('since', ''))} – {fmt_date(data.get('until', ''))}"
    x = pill(d, x + int(10 * S), cy, dates, fchip, S, outline=LINE, color=WHITE)
    if data.get("replies") is not None:
        n = f"{int(data['replies']):,} replies"
        meta = ("Sampled · " + n) if data.get("sampled") else n
    else:
        meta = data.get("note", "")
    if meta:
        d.text((x + int(16 * S), cy), meta, font=font(int(16 * S), "Medium"), fill=DIM, anchor="lm")
    # tier rows
    lw = max(1, int(S * 1.5)); bs = int(52 * S)
    for t, y, h in L["rows"]:
        d.line((pad, y, W - pad, y), fill=LINE, width=lw)
        cx, cyy = pad + L["lab"] // 2 - int(6 * S), y + h // 2
        box = (cx - bs // 2, cyy - bs // 2, cx + bs // 2, cyy + bs // 2)
        if t == "S":
            d.rounded_rectangle(box, int(14 * S), fill=BLUE)
            d.text((cx, cyy), t, font=font(int(30 * S), "Black"), fill=(255, 255, 255), anchor="mm")
        else:
            d.rounded_rectangle(box, int(14 * S), outline=LINE, width=lw)
            d.text((cx, cyy), t, font=font(int(30 * S), "Black"), fill=WHITE, anchor="mm")
    y_end = L["rows"][-1][1] + L["rows"][-1][2]
    d.line((pad, y_end, W - pad, y_end), fill=LINE, width=lw)
    fy = H - int(38 * S); ff = font(int(15 * S), "Medium")
    d.text((pad, fy), f"Top {len(L['slots'])} accounts · ranked by replies sent", font=ff, fill=DIM, anchor="lm")
    spaced(d, (W - pad - int(1 * S) - sum(d.textlength(c, font=ff) + int(1.5 * S) for c in "X REPLY TIERLIST"), fy),
           "X REPLY TIERLIST", font(int(15 * S), "SemiBold"), DIM, int(1.5 * S))
    return img

def tile_img(hd, c, av, L):
    """Avatar + handle caption as RGBA sprite."""
    S, t = L["S"], L["tile"]; capH = max(int(22 * S), int(t * .22)); cw = t + int(min(L.get("gap", 8 * S) - 2 * S, 22 * S))
    sp = Image.new("RGBA", (cw, t + capH), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    sp.paste(av, ((cw - t) // 2, 0), round_mask(t, int(16 * S)))
    ImageDraw.Draw(sp).rounded_rectangle(((cw - t) // 2, 0, (cw - t) // 2 + t - 1, t - 1), int(16 * S),
                                         outline=LINE + (255,), width=max(1, int(S)))  # hairline edge
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(sp); s = "@" + hd; fs = max(int(12 * S), int(t * .13))
    while d.textlength(s, font=font(fs, "Medium")) > cw and fs > int(10 * S): fs -= 1
    if d.textlength(s, font=font(fs, "Medium")) > cw:
        while d.textlength(s + "…", font=font(fs, "Medium")) > cw: s = s[:-1]
        s += "…"
    cap_col = tuple(int(a * .82 + b * .18) for a, b in zip(WHITE, BLACK))
    d.text((cw / 2, t + capH * .55), s, font=font(fs, "Medium"), fill=cap_col, anchor="mm")
    return sp

def render(data, out="tierlist", size=None, theme=None, gif=True):
    """size: 48 / 60 people (6 full rows of 8 / 10), square output. theme: "dark" / "light".
    Both can also come from the JSON ("size", "theme"); "exclude": [handles] drops accounts."""
    global PER_ROW, MAX_PEOPLE
    size = int(size or data.get("size") or 60)
    size = min(SIZES, key=lambda k: abs(k - size))
    PER_ROW, MAX_PEOPLE = SIZES[size], size
    set_theme((theme or data.get("theme") or "dark").lower())
    ex = {h.lower().lstrip("@") for h in data.get("exclude", [])}
    data = dict(data, ranked=[r for r in data["ranked"] if r[0].lower() not in ex])
    L = layout(data, 1.0)
    handles = [hd for _, hd, *_ in L["slots"]]
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
        avs = dict(zip(handles, ex.map(lambda h: avatar(h, 300), handles)))
    failed = [h for h, (_, ok) in avs.items() if not ok]
    # PNG
    img = base(data, L)
    for t, hd, c, x, y in L["slots"]:
        sp = tile_img(hd, c, avs[hd][0].resize((L["tile"],) * 2, Image.LANCZOS), L)
        img.paste(sp, (x - (sp.width - L["tile"]) // 2, y), sp)
    img.save(out + ".png", optimize=True)
    info = {"png": out + ".png", "failed_avatars": failed,
            "tiers": {t: [f"@{hd} ({c})" for tt, hd, c, *_ in L["slots"] if tt == t] for t in TIERS}}
    if not gif:
        return info
    # GIF (half scale, avatars drop in from F up to S)
    G = layout(data, 0.6); bg = base(data, G)
    sprites = {hd: tile_img(hd, c, avs[hd][0].resize((G["tile"],) * 2, Image.LANCZOS), G)
               for _, hd, c, *_ in G["slots"]}
    order = sorted(G["slots"], key=lambda s: (-TIERS.index(s[0]), -s[3]))
    fps, drop = 20, 7                      # 7 frames per fall
    n = len(order); span = 56              # frames over which drops start
    starts = [int(i * span / max(1, n - 1)) if n > 1 else 0 for i in range(n)]
    # S tier gets a short pause before it lands
    s_idx = [i for i, s in enumerate(order) if s[0] == "S"]
    for i in s_idx: starts[i] += 6
    total = max(starts) + drop + 1
    frames = []
    for f in range(total):
        fr = bg.copy()
        for (t, hd, c, x, y), st in zip(order, starts):
            k = f - st
            if k < 0: continue
            p = min(1, k / drop); e = 1 - (1 - p) ** 3
            if p < 1:

            fr.paste(sprites[hd], (x - (sprites[hd].width - G["tile"]) // 2, yy), sprites[hd])

    q = [fr.quantize(palette=pal, dither=Image.Dither.NONE) for fr in frames]
```
